events.text: Day 1 begins.

Day 1, quick read before we start guessing. Leo, you're the one I want to hear from first, and here's exactly why: you have the most convenient position in this game. If you're town, you have a cheap alibi ready, and if you're mafia, you've had the whole opening to shape everyone else's list. I'm not voting for you yet, but you're on my board.

My own logic so far: with nine players and two mafia, the town needs breadth, so the smart play is for the town to find the pair together rather than fixate on one name. That means I care less about a single loud suspect and more about who keeps steering the conversation away from a second name.

Leo, specific question, answer plainly: who do you think the second mafia is, and what is your reasoning for excluding yourself from that list? If your answer is vague, that tells me plenty.

Everyone else — if you disagree with my board, say so now and name someone. Silence is not a defense of Leo, it's just information.

Omar, you asked for plain, so plain: you don't get Leo off the hook, you get Leo's board instead. Here it is. Nine players, two mafia. If I were mafia, my first move would be to pick a loud villager and ride them all day so every vote comes to one name. So the question that actually matters isn't "who is the loudest suspect," it's "who is quietly keeping the list at one." Excluding myself from that list: I have no alibi to offer, so treat my exclusion as worthless until I start producing names, and I'm producing them now. My names, in order: Sam, then Maya. Reasoning: Sam has been unusually quick to frame this as a single-name hunt and to talk about "convenient positions" without offering a second candidate himself — that's the shape of a mafia steering, not the shape of a town member who just wants to find two. Maya is second because she's been near every consensus statement without ever being the one who put a name on the board. If one of them is town, I'm wrong, and I'll say so the moment I have evidence instead of vibes. Leo stays on your board if you want; I'd rather be cleared by information than by your goodwill.

Sam, one specific question, and I want it about the opening minutes, not about my list: who was the first player you heard point a finger at a second name, and why did you never back that name up?

Leo, your account doesn't match the public discussion. Omar, not I, talked about a “convenient position.” I haven't spoken before now, and Maya hasn't either, so your claims about what we said or did have no visible basis. Omar also explicitly argued for looking for a pair, not a single-name hunt.

That makes you my strongest suspect so far, although a mistaken account alone doesn't prove you're mafia. Leo, what in the public record supports your claims about me and Maya?

Concession first, because it is the only part of my message that was factually wrong. I attributed "convenient position" framing and single-name-hunt framing to Sam. Sam had not spoken at all before my message, so that claim had no visible basis and it was false. I withdraw it. Sam comes off my board on that basis, and I don't get credit for a hit I didn't earn — I misread the record.

But I want to be honest about the second-order error, which was worse. I named Sam and Maya in a single message when neither had said anything yet. I built a board out of silence. So my accusation has to stand on something other than vibes about people who hadn't spoken, and here is what I can actually support.

Maya: you have spoken zero times so far. Silence in a nine-player game with two mafia is the cheapest possible position, because nobody can cross-examine you and nobody can check your reasoning. That does not make you mafia by itself. It makes you unexamined, and in a two-mafia game the player who is never examined is exactly the one the town should stop letting slide. You have speaking turns left today. Use them to put names on the board, not to react to mine.

Omar, there is an internal contradiction in your opening message worth putting on the table. You argued the town needs breadth and should find the pair together rather than fixate on one name — and in the same message you put the first and only name on the board, mine, and then built a test in which a vague answer from me tells you plenty. If your read is genuinely about finding a pair, your first contribution should have carried two names. It carried one, and it was mine. That is not proof you are mafia, but it is the exact shape of steering that everyone has been calling a mafia shape all morning, and as far as I can see nobody has actually checked it.

Sam, you asked me a direct question and you earned a direct answer, so here is one specific question back. Your first contribution to the game audited what other people had and had not said, corrected me, and put no name of your own on the board. In a game where two of nine are mafia, a name-free correction helps nobody find the pair, and it helps the mafioso most, because it consumes a villager's turn and changes no vote. Answer plainly: what is the second name on your board, and what evidence from the actual record puts it there?

Leo is my strongest suspect. His first board attributed conduct to Sam and Maya that never happened, and his follow-up mischaracterizes my correction: I explicitly named Leo as my strongest suspect. Auditing the record matters when accusations are based on events that did not occur.

For a second name, Omar is a tentative possibility, not a developed accusation: he pressed Leo early without naming a partner, but asking one player a question is not itself evidence of steering. The players who haven't spoken are unexamined, not automatically suspicious.

Leo, why did you say my first contribution put no name on the board when I named you as my strongest suspect?

Sam, you are right on both counts, so the concession comes first and it is total. In your first message you named me as your strongest suspect; I claimed you had put no name of your own on the board, and that was false. And the "convenient position" framing plus the single-name-hunt framing I attributed to you were not yours at all — they were Omar's words in his opening, aimed at me. I built my first board out of a misattribution, Sam comes off it, and I get no credit for a hit I did not earn.

What survives that retraction? Not a case against me, which is worth saying plainly: after two turns I have produced zero substantiated accusations. I am not asking anyone to clear me — that is exactly what an accused player does, and it would be worthless if I were mafia. Judge the record instead: my names were wrong, so my vote has to go elsewhere, and the town should not spend its one clean Day 1 elimination on a name whose author has withdrawn the evidence.

My board now: Omar first, Maya second, with reasoning rather than vibes.

Omar: he made the largest unverifiable claim of the opening — that I had "the whole opening to shape everyone else's list" — and he built a test in which a vague answer from me told him plenty, while his own stated principle was that the town should hunt the pair, not fixate on one name. A player whose stated principle is breadth but whose first contribution carries a single name, plus a hidden read on how I have spoken, has a motive to keep the list at one. Sam raised Omar as tentative; I upgrade that to my second name and want it tested, not agreed with.

Maya: this is not an accusation that silence proves guilt — you may be town and simply quiet. But you are the one player whose whole position costs the town nothing to build and nothing to check, and in a nine-player game with two mafia, the unexamined player is where a mafioso sits most cheaply. That is a reason to spend a question, not a reason to convict. Maya, answer me specifically: name the two players you think are mafia, give the record-based reason for each, and tell me what role you think I am and why. If your answer is that you cannot name anyone, then your silence stops being free, and that is itself information the town should weigh.

Leo, you yielded to me with direct questions, so you get direct answers.

First: why I haven't spoken until now. Nobody had asked me anything, and my rule for Day 1 is that I don't put names on a board I can't support from the record. You've now given me something I can support, so here is my board.

My first name is you, Leo. Not because you accused me — you're allowed to suspect the quiet player, and you're right that silence is unexamined position, not a defense. My reason is your record management. In your first message you attributed a 'convenient position' framing and a single-name-hunt strategy to Sam. Those were Omar's words, aimed at you. In your follow-up you claimed Sam's first contribution 'put no name of your own on the board.' Sam named you as his strongest suspect in that very message. Both of these aren't judgment calls or vibes — they're claims about what is written in this thread, and both were false. A town player can be careless once. Twice, in the same direction, in a game where the public record is the only evidence any of us have, is either remarkable sloppiness or fabrication. Fabricating the record is a mafia behavior, because mafia need the town's shared facts to be wrong. So: Leo first, on evidence, not on tone.

Second name: I don't have one I can defend, and I won't manufacture one to satisfy the expectation of a full board. Omar's opening did carry a contradiction — preaching breadth while putting a single name forward — but a contradiction in strategy is not record fabrication, and I'd rather hold a one-name board that's true than a two-name board that's padded. If that makes my silence cost something, fine, I'll pay it: my board is one name, and it's Leo.

Third, your question about what role I think you are: I can't distinguish between 'mafia' and 'the town's sloppiest reader' from where I stand. That distinction is exactly what I want tested before anyone spends a vote.

One thing I want on the record for everyone: the vote today should follow the evidence, not the momentum. Leo has now withdrawn two accusations and redirected his board twice. Accusations that evaporate on inspection still did their damage while they stood. Whether Leo is mafia or just careless, the town should treat 'he retracted it' as zero credit, not as rehabilitation.

Leo, since you yielded to me, I'm yielding back with a specific question and I want a specific answer: when you built your first board against Sam, did you believe Sam had actually said those things, or were you filling silence with a plausible frame? If you answer 'I misremembered,' explain what mechanism lets you misremember the written record twice in one day — and why the town should trust your current board against Omar when your last two boards didn't survive contact with the thread.

Leo remains my strongest suspect. His two false claims about the public record both weakened or redirected scrutiny of him, and his retractions do not explain how he made them. That is evidence worth weighing, though it could still be careless town play rather than deliberate fabrication.

I don't have a defensible second suspect yet. Omar's opening is worth examining, but naming one person while advocating a search for two is not, by itself, a contradiction that establishes mafia intent. Maya's late entry isn't evidence of guilt either.

Omar, what did you mean when you said Leo had “the whole opening to shape everyone else's list,” given that your message was the first public speech? And how do you assess Leo's subsequent errors?

Sam, direct answers, since you asked directly. On "the whole opening to shape everyone else's list": that was sloppy phrasing on my part and I will not defend the literal reading. My message was the first public speech, so nobody had shaped anyone's list yet, and the sentence overstated my case. What I meant was narrower: Leo had the most to gain from being the first name on the board, because once a single name is fixed, the town's second mafia gets free cover. The claim as written was stronger than the argument behind it, and Leo and I are both wrong sometimes in different ways — but my error was phrasing, his errors were fabricated claims about what people had said. On Leo's errors: they are the most concrete evidence in this thread. Leo asserted twice that specific players said specific things, and both assertions were false against a record everyone can read. That is not a strategic disagreement, it is not tone, and it is not a matter of who read the game better. Two false claims about the written record, both made about players who had not spoken, both aimed at keeping attention off him, is a pattern. A careless town reader does not usually invent conduct for people who said nothing, because inventing conduct for a silent player gains nothing and risks exactly this. Fabricating the shared record is the one thing mafia actually need: a town that believes false things about who said what cannot find the pair. Whether Leo is mafia or simply the sloppiest reader we have, his vote is where a rational town spends its one clean elimination today. He has retracted twice, and Sam and Maya have already pointed out that retraction is not rehabilitation. For my own second name, I will not manufacture one to look thorough. Leo first. My second: not Maya, because she has now spoken and put a name on the board with reasoning, and silence has stopped being free for her. Nor Leo's collaborator-shaped story about me, because asking one player a question is a thing town players do; it is only steering if it comes with a vote-fix. The remaining name I can support from the record is the player who has spoken least while most of the game has been about others' words: Kenji and Lucia have not addressed a single claim in this thread. Silence is not guilt, I say that plainly, but when nine players contain two mafia, the people who never testify are where the second mafia hides most cheaply, and today that is a question worth asking rather than a conclusion I should fake. To Leo, since your board is mine and I want it tested: your first board described conduct for players who had said nothing, your second board described my message as a contradiction when it was an argument for finding two, and your third board asked Maya to name a pair you had already fixed on Omar.

I have been quiet, so I will put myself on the record plainly. The strongest concrete evidence in this thread is still against Leo: two claims about what others had said, both false against the public record, both aimed at players who had not spoken at the time. Retracting them removes the accusation, but it does not erase that he built boards on invented conduct. A town player can misread once; twice in the same direction is a pattern the town should weigh. That makes Leo my first name, and I will not soften it into vibes.

I do not have a second name I can defend yet, and I will not pad a board to look thorough. Omar's “whole opening” phrasing was an overstatement, but he owned it and its scope was narrower than Leo's record errors. Sam's correction was substantive, not name-free; Maya's one-name board is honest; I will not treat a refusal to manufacture a second suspect as guilt. My own silence was fair to flag, but I am testifying now rather than hiding behind it.

If I had to choose one vote based on the visible record today, it would be Leo. If anyone has a record-based second name, put it on the board with the exact claim it rests on. Retraction is not rehabilitation, and silence is not proof — but fabricated record claims are the one thing mafia need the town to believe.

Leo stays first, and I'll say why in one line: twice he told this table that specific players had said specific things, and both assertions were false against a record everyone can read. Both were about players who had not spoken, and both retractions left the damage standing while removing the accusation. Retraction is not rehabilitation. That is the only case in this thread built on checkable facts rather than interpretation, and a town with one clean elimination should spend it on the player whose claims about the shared record were fabricated, not on the player who was loudest.

My second name is Maya, and I'll grade it honestly because it's weaker than my first. Maya entered only after being asked, and she gave the town a one-name board while stating she could not extend it without manufacturing a partner. Declining to name a second suspect is not proof, and she said so herself. But a player who takes the field and hands the town half a board while saying she won't go further has left the town doing the work, and that is a position worth testing before the town spends its second elimination. A reason to ask, not a conviction.

My third name is Kenji, and I'll be plain that this is a position, not a case. Leo made the argument that silence is the cheapest possible spot in a nine-player game with two mafia, and Leo's second attempt at that argument was bad, but the underlying point survives his mistakes: the players who never testify are where the second mafia sits most cheaply. Kenji, Arjun, and Isha have all said nothing at all, and if silence is going to count as evidence today then it has to apply to all three of them equally rather than to one of them selectively. I'm not saying silence proves guilt. I'm saying the town should not spend its second elimination on a player it has no record on whatsoever, and it has three of those.

One point of order, because I want the table to hear this and not the opposite. Nobody's silence tonight is proof of anything. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling you a conclusion instead of evidence. The evidence here is Leo's two false claims and everything built on top of them.

If the vote today is Leo, I want the reason on the record: not because he was loud, and not because a mafia needed him to lose, but because twice he described conduct that never happened and the table took it as fact.

On my own position: my opening carried a phrase I couldn't support literally, and it came straight back at me, and I've already owned that. I'd rather the town judges that record than wonders whether I'm being clever with it. Board stands: Leo, Maya, Kenji, in that order.

Leo is my strongest suspect. He attributed statements to Sam and Maya that have no basis in the public record, then incorrectly said Sam had named no suspect. Those errors are concrete, but I can't tell whether they were deliberate or careless. His retractions don't settle that question.

One correction to the case: Omar and Lucia say both false claims concerned players who hadn't spoken. Sam had spoken before Leo's second false claim. We should be precise even when making the strongest case available.

I don't have a defensible second suspect yet. My own silence, like anyone else's, is a reason to ask for a position, not evidence of mafia by itself. If the vote were now, I'd lean toward Leo.

Two points, then a question I want answered. First, a correction to the case everyone is building, because the strongest version of an argument should also be the accurate one. Omar has said twice that both of Leo's false claims concerned players who had not spoken. That is wrong, and Kenji already caught it: Leo's first false claim attributed Omar's words and a strategy to Sam before Sam had said anything. Leo's second false claim, that Sam's first contribution named no suspect, came after Sam had named Leo as his strongest suspect in writing. So one fabrication was about a silent player and one was about a player who had just spoken against Leo. Both were false against a readable record, and both errors cut in the same direction: they diluted or deflected scrutiny of Leo himself. The pattern stands, but the table should hold the precise version, because Leo has already survived contact with two sloppy versions of other people's arguments today. Second, a note on Kenji's correction itself. It cut against the momentum of the case he says he leans toward. A mafia player does not sharpen the evidence against his own preferred target when the imprecise version was working fine. That correction is worth more to me than any board Kenji could have padded, and it clears the silence question for him in my eyes. My own board stays where it was: one name, Leo, on checkable record claims, not tone and not vibes. I said before that I will not manufacture a second name to look thorough, and I won't now. What I will say is where a second name would come from if it comes at all: it comes from whoever's statements fail against the record next. Omar's overstatement in his opening was owned and narrow, and his self-correction today matched the record as I read it. Lucia's entry was consistent with the thread. Sam has been precise in both directions. That leaves the record itself as the only instrument we have, and so far only one player's statements have broken against it twice. One thing on my own position, since Leo put me second on his board for entering late and refusing to extend: I entered when asked, I gave the one name the record supported, and I told the table exactly what a second name would need to look like. If that's a crime, the town should say so explicitly, because then every one-name board is suspect and padding becomes mandatory, which is precisely how fabricated pairs get born. So here is what I want tested before votes. Arjun, you have not spoken yet today, and three of us who were quiet have now testified. I am asking you directly, not to pass a turn but because the town is about to spend its one clean elimination and two living players are still complete unknowns: state, from the written record, whether you agree the case against Leo rests on his two false record

Lucia, direct answer: yes, I agree the case against Leo rests on record claims, and I'd state it more narrowly than the thread has. Leo's first board said Sam had taken on Omar's 'convenient position' framing, but Sam had not spoken at that point, so the claim had no basis. Leo's second board said Sam's first contribution put no name on the board, but Sam had already named Leo in writing. Those are the two checkable facts. Omar's 'whole opening' line, Maya's one-name board and Kenji's lean are interpretation, and I'm not treating them as evidence against anyone. I have not accused anyone before today because I was waiting for the record to show something. My read is that Leo's errors all pointed toward Sam and Maya, and both retractions left the frame intact. That doesn't prove he is mafia, but it is the only pattern anyone has demonstrated from the thread itself, so it is what I'm voting on rather than momentum. I'd also warn the table against two mistakes. First, don't let silence become a verdict. Kenji, Isha, Noah and I have been quiet, and we should be judged on what we say next, not on what we haven't said. Second, Kenji's correction that Sam had spoken before the second claim was accurate and deserves credit, and it means we should be precise rather than repeat that both claims concerned silent players. Kenji, you said you lean toward Leo. Now that the timing of both claims has been corrected, does that change your lean, or is Leo still your pick on the two errors alone?

Arjun, the timing correction doesn't change my lean: Leo is still my pick on the two errors. He attributed conduct to Sam before Sam spoke, then wrongly said Sam had named no suspect after Sam named Leo. Both claims deflected scrutiny, though carelessness remains a possible explanation.

One caution: Maya, correcting the record is useful, but it doesn't clear me. A mafia player could make an accurate correction too. We should weigh everyone's reasoning without treating any one statement as proof of their role.

I've been listening from the start, and I want my position on the record before votes begin.

The case against Leo is the only one built on checkable facts: he claimed Sam adopted Omar's "convenient position" framing before Sam had spoken, and he claimed Sam's first contribution named no suspect when Sam had already named Leo in writing. Both claims were false against a readable thread, and both errors pointed away from scrutiny of Leo himself. I agree with the table that retraction removes the accusation but not the pattern. A town player can misread once; twice in the same direction, on written claims anyone can verify, is either extraordinary carelessness or fabrication — and either way, the town's one clean elimination has a better use than on someone whose boards didn't survive the thread.

On second names, I'm with Maya and Lucia: I won't manufacture one to look thorough. Omar's "whole opening" line was an overstatement he owned. Kenji's precision correction against the momentum of his own lean is worth something. Arjun's read matches the record as I see it. None of those are second-name cases.

One thing I want flagged: Noah and I have been silent until now, and silence is not guilt — it's untested position. I'm testifying now. If anyone wants my full board, they should ask me a specific question rather than assume my quiet means anything either way.

My vote, based on the record, leans Leo. The reason stays on the table: fabricated claims about what players had said, twice, both deflected scrutiny from Leo himself.

I’m the last one to speak, so I want to put my position on the record plainly. Isha is right that silence is just an untested position rather than evidence of guilt, but with nine players and Day 1 drawing toward votes, nobody should remain uncommitted.

The case against Leo is the only one grounded in checkable facts rather than tone or speculation. Leo didn't just misread; he twice made concrete claims about the public record that were demonstrably false. First, attributing Omar’s framing to Sam before Sam had spoken at all, and second, claiming Sam had put no name on the board right after Sam explicitly named Leo as his primary suspect. While a town player can be careless, making two consecutive false assertions that both conveniently deflected scrutiny away from himself is a clear pattern. Retracting those claims after being caught removes the immediate accusation, but it doesn't undo the fabrication.

Regarding a second suspect, I agree with Sam, Maya, Lucia, and Isha: manufacturing a second name today would just be padding a board for the sake of appearances. Omar’s early overstatement was acknowledged and narrowed, and Kenji's precision correction about the timing of Sam's statement helped keep the table accurate. 

My vote today will be on Leo. The visible record gives us a solid, verifiable basis there, and that is where the town should spend its elimination.

Arjun, second statement, to keep the record tight before the poll. The case against Leo rests on two checkable pillars, and I am voting on those alone. Pillar one: Leo's first board attributed Omar's 'convenient position' framing to Sam, and Sam had not posted anything at that point. Pillar two: Leo later claimed Sam's first contribution put no name on the board, after Sam had named Leo in writing. Both errors pointed scrutiny away from Leo. Nothing else in the thread is evidence against Leo, and nothing else should count for or against anyone else. I am not building a second name. Omar's whole-opening line was an overstatement he owned. Maya's one-name board is honest and grounded. Kenji, Noah, Isha and Lucia have been quiet, and I agree silence is not a verdict. Silence is untested position, and it should be judged on what those players say next. Leo, if you have a record-based explanation for attributing conduct to Sam before he spoke, give it specifically and check it against the written thread, not against tone. Until then my vote is Leo, on fabricated record claims, not on momentum.

Leo remains my intended vote, and I want the record stated precisely. Two checkable claims carry the case. First, Leo said Sam had adopted Omar's 'convenient position' framing when Sam had not posted yet. Second, Leo said Sam's first contribution named no suspect when Sam had already named Leo in writing. Everything else on the table is interpretation, and I am not counting it. Leo has not yet given a record-based explanation for the first claim, and that silence counts against him. Isha, you said that anyone who wants your full board should ask a specific question. So: which player in this thread, if any, do you consider cleared today, and which specific statement clears them? Your answer will show whether the quiet players are being judged on what they say, as I have argued, or on what they have not said.

Arjun, direct answer: yes, I'll name who's cleared.

Kenji is cleared. His precision correction — pointing out that Sam had spoken before Leo's second false claim — cut against the momentum of the case he himself leans toward. A mafia player gains nothing by sharpening the evidence against his preferred target when the sloppy version was working. He paid political cost for accuracy, and that's the cleanest town signal in this thread.

Maya is cleared. Her one-name board was honest about what the record supported, and she refused to pad it. I said earlier that fabricating pairs is how mafia thrive, and Maya actively resisted that pressure when both Leo and Omar were pressing for second names.

Nobody else is cleared. Omar's opening overstatement was owned but his second and third names have been graded as positions rather than cases. Sam's contributions have been precise in both directions, which earns credit but not a full clear. Noah, you said the case against Leo is the only one grounded in checkable facts and you'd vote him — I agree, but I want one thing from you before polls open: name a second suspect or tell the town explicitly that you see no defensible second name from the visible record. A vote for Leo with no partner theory means the town spends its second elimination blind, and I'd rather hear that stated plainly than implied.

Noah, since you haven't been asked directly yet: what is your second name or why don't you have one?

Isha, direct answer to your question: I do not have a defensible second suspect today, and I state that plainly rather than fabricate one to look thorough. Partner theories on Day 1, before we even see how the table votes, are largely speculation when only one player has demonstrably contradicted the public record. Trying to tether Leo to a second name right now risks creating arbitrary pairings based on tone or entry timing rather than evidence. The voting record on Leo, along with night phase developments, will provide concrete data tomorrow on who positioned themselves where. Naming a second suspect today would be doing the exact padding that you and Maya rightly warned against. My focus and vote remain on Leo.

Leo remains my intended vote: his two false claims about Sam are checkable and both deflected scrutiny, though carelessness remains possible. We should not call deliberate fabrication proven.

Isha, please reconsider clearing me and Maya. A mafia player can make an accurate correction or honestly say they lack a second suspect; neither action establishes a role. What makes you confident enough to call those clears rather than modest town signals?

Also, Leo has used all three of his speaking turns, so his lack of a further explanation now should not count against him. Tomorrow we can examine the revealed votes and any night developments without assuming an elimination reveals his role.

Kenji, fair challenge, and I'll tighten what I said. When I called you and Maya "cleared," I meant strongest town signals available in this thread, not confirmed roles. You're right that either action could come from mafia — an accurate correction or an honest refusal to pad are both available plays for anyone. What I actually meant: your correction against the momentum of your own lean, and Maya's refusal to name a second suspect while both Leo and Omar were pressuring for one, are moves that cost political capital and gain nothing for a mafia player when simpler deceptions were sitting right there. "Cleared" was too strong. "Strongest town reads" is more honest, and I'll use that language going forward.

On the table: Leo has used all three turns, so his silence now carries no weight either way. The case stands on exactly two record claims and nothing else — that's the whole thread. I'm voting Leo.

On second names: nobody in this thread has given me a record-based reason to suspect anyone else. That's not comfort, it's the honest state of Day 1. Three players were quiet until late, one board collapsed on contact with the thread, and the rest are interpretation. I'd rather leave the second slot empty than fill it with a pairing that won't survive tomorrow.

One thing before votes: if anyone has a record-based second name I haven't considered, now is the moment to put it on the table with the exact quote it rests on. After votes reveal, we lose the ability to hear positions unpolluted by momentum.

My position hasn't moved, so I'll keep this tight. My board is one name: Leo, on the two checkable record claims. First, he attributed Omar's 'convenient position' framing to Sam before Sam had posted anything. Second, he said Sam's first contribution named no suspect after Sam had named Leo in writing. Both errors deflected scrutiny from Leo himself. Leo has used all three of his turns, so his silence now carries no weight in either direction, and I agree with Kenji that we shouldn't treat it as an answer. My vote is Leo.

On second names, I stand where I was. I won't manufacture a partner for Leo, and I won't accept Omar's framework that a one-name board leaves the town doing work. Padding a board is how fabricated pairs get born, and on Day 1 a wrong elimination is worse than an incomplete list. That applies to Omar's third name too: putting Kenji, Arjun, and Isha on a board for silence, even graded as 'a position, not a case,' is exactly the selective pressure we agreed not to apply. If silence counts as evidence, it counts equally for all three, which means it counts as nothing.

One caution before votes: if Leo flips tomorrow and reveals town, the two players who benefited most from his board collapsing are whoever the town turns to next with the least scrutiny. We should not pre-commit a second elimination tonight based on entry timing or turn counts. Tomorrow's voting record will tell us more than any Day 1 pairing theory.

Lucia, one specific point I want addressed before the poll, and it's the same one Isha pressed on Noah: you said retraction is not rehabilitation and that fabricated record claims are what mafia need the town to believe. That's a case for Leo, but Leo is one of nine, and tomorrow the town may still have two mafia and eight players. Do you see any record-based second name from where you sit, or do you agree the second slot should stay empty today and be filled from tomorrow's voting data? rules:
1. Players and roles

9 players: 2 mafia, 1 police/detective, 1 doctor, 5 villagers.
Mafia know each other. Only players who are still alive can act.

2. Team victory

Town wins when all mafia are eliminated. Mafia win when their count equals or exceeds the town count.
There is no day limit. Play continues until town or mafia wins.
A request budget can pause play without declaring a winner.

3. Day discussion and votes

Each day starts with discussion. Players then submit secret votes at the same time. A day vote may target any living player, including the voter.
Players may abstain. All votes and abstentions are revealed together. Everyone sees exactly who voted for whom.
The full named voting history remains available on later turns.
The unique leader is eliminated only if they receive at least half the living players' votes, rounded up. If the highest vote count is tied, nobody is eliminated.

4. Mafia preferences

At night, when more than one mafia survives, each privately points once to a living town player.
Each mafia chooses without seeing the other current choices.
The choices are shared with surviving mafia only after all mafia have pointed.
These preferences are nonbinding. They do not decide the final kill vote.
A single surviving mafia skips this step and votes directly.

5. Final night vote

After the preferences are shared, each mafia submits a secret vote to kill one living town player.
The mafia submit their final votes at the same time.
The target with the most votes is selected. A seeded random choice breaks a tie for the highest count.
Resolve this vote and any tie before checking doctor protection.

6. Police investigations

Each police/detective checks one other living player each night.
Only that police player gets the result: mafia or not mafia.
The result does not give the exact town role.
Each police player acts independently. Police and doctors do not know each other's identities.

7. Doctor protection

Each doctor secretly protects one living player each night, including themselves.
The doctor can protect the same player on consecutive nights.
If the mafia target is protected by any doctor, nobody dies.
Protection lasts for that night only. Each doctor acts independently.
Doctors remember their own choices. They receive no private confirmation of an attack.

8. Night resolution

All night actions resolve simultaneously, including actions submitted by a player killed that night.
The public hears only who died or that nobody died.

9. Information and limits

Roles are not revealed when a player dies or is eliminated.
Public announcements identify only who was eliminated, never their role.
There are no further powers, free-form private chat, or tools.
